findings.title: A broad 'view all clients' grant short-circuits per-client deny permissions in canView(client)
findings.body: `canView(ClientModel)` first returns true if `canView()` is true. `canView()` is true when the caller holds the VIEW scope on the all-clients (type) resource (`hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)`). Only afterwards does it consult the per-client resource. The same applies to `canConfigure(client)`, which is also reached from this short-circuit. A per-client permission with negative logic, or any per-client policy that should deny VIEW for one client, is therefore never evaluated once an all-clients VIEW permission exists. The Users tests (`testViewUserPermission`) treat 'allow all, deny one' as supported behaviour. Here the deny is silently ignored, so the caller can view and list a client they were explicitly denied. No test covers this case for clients.

findings.title: getResourceName has no branch for the new Clients resource type
findings.body: `getResourceName` maps resource names to display names only for `USERS`. The `Users` branch turns the user id into a username and returns 'All users' for the type resource. The new `Clients` type is not handled. A per-client resource is named by the client's internal UUID (see `getOrCreateResource`/`resolveClient`) and has no display name, so it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Clients permissions then show a null or meaningless name for per-client resources, and 'Clients' instead of an 'All clients' label for the type resource. Add a `CLIENTS` branch that resolves the client id to its clientId and returns 'All clients' for the type resource.

findings.title: Possible NPE when the Clients type resource does not exist
findings.body: When no per-client resource exists, `getResourceTypeResource(...)` is called and its result is passed straight to `PolicyStore.findByResource(server, resource)`. That method returns null when the schema is not active (for example admin permissions disabled on the realm while the client remains), or when the 'Clients' resource was never created. The second case applies to any realm whose admin-permissions client was created before this change, because `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` returns early if the client already exists and never adds the new Clients scopes or resource. This path runs for every ordinary client access check, so it would turn those checks into 500s instead of a plain 'false'. Add a null check on `resource` before using it.

findings.title: UnsupportedOperationException is thrown from methods reachable via public admin and token-exchange paths
findings.body: `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns a `ClientPermissionsV2` whose `canExchangeTo`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `getPermissions`, `resource` and the `*Permission(client)` methods all throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. These are the V1 methods called from existing code. One caller is the client `management/permissions` REST endpoint. Another is the legacy token-exchange check, which calls `canExchangeTo`. With V2 enabled these requests now fail with an uncaught exception, a 500, instead of a 403/404 or a 'permissions disabled' response. Before this change the inherited V1 behaviour returned a normal answer. Either return safe values (false / disabled / empty) or guard those endpoints for V2.

findings.title: Gating the removal listener on V1 leaves orphaned V2 permission resources when clients, roles or groups are deleted
findings.body: The listener that disables permissions on role, client and group removal now runs only when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` (V1) is enabled. This avoids calling the throwing V2 `setPermissionsEnabled`. But nothing replaces it for V2. When a client is deleted, its per-client resource (named by client id) and any scope permissions that reference it stay in the admin-permissions resource server as stale data. Deleting a client that has per-client permissions therefore leaves dangling resources and permissions. V2 needs a cleanup on `ClientRemovedEvent`, or this gap should be called out explicitly.

findings.title: Javadoc of void require* methods describes a boolean return
findings.body: `requireView()` and `requireViewClientScopes()` are void methods that throw `ForbiddenException`. Their new Javadoc says 'Returns {@code true} if canView() returns true' and 'Returns {@code true} if canViewClientScopes() returns true'. Every other require* method in this file says 'Throws ForbiddenException if ...'. The text misleads callers about the contract and should be changed to the 'Throws ForbiddenException if ... returns false' form.

findings.title: Dead code and unused imports left in new class
findings.body: `getEvaluationContext(...)` is private and never called. The `logger` field and the imports `Scope`, `TOKEN_EXCHANGE`, `ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext`, `EvaluationContext` and `AccessToken` (used only by the dead method and `canExchangeTo`) are leftovers from the V1 token-exchange code. They add noise and suggest functionality that does not exist in V2. Remove them.

findings.title: Test rotates the secret of the client that the admin client authenticates with
findings.body: `testConfigureOnlyOneClient` calls `clientResource.generateNewSecret()` on `myclient`. The injected `realmAdminClient` authenticates as `myclient` with secret `mysecret`. After rotation, `mysecret` no longer authenticates, because no rotation policy is configured. Any later test in the class that needs a fresh or refreshed token (token expiry, a re-created admin client) would get 401 depending on execution order and timing. The test state is also not restored in cleanup. Use a different client for the secret operations, or restore the secret afterwards.

findings.title: Missing coverage for map-roles-client-scope, deny semantics and the all-clients/per-client interplay
findings.body: The new schema adds `map-roles-client-scope`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` is implemented, but no test exercises it. There is also no test of a negative per-client permission combined with an all-clients VIEW/MANAGE grant, which is where `canView(client)` currently misbehaves. There is no test of `getClientsWithPermission`. The tests only check positive grants on one client, or on all clients, in isolation.
